title: Measles-exposed Amtrak traveler rode through six California counties
excerpt: An unvaccinated passenger later hospitalized with measles traveled by train and bus through six counties Sept. 12–14; L.A. Union Station visitors from Saturday 8 a.m.–noon should monitor symptoms through Oct. 3.
body:
• An unvaccinated traveler, later hospitalized with confirmed measles, rode Amtrak trains and Thruway buses through Alameda, Butte, Kern, Los Angeles, Sacramento and San Joaquin counties from Sept. 12 to 14.
  • The passenger arrived at L.A.'s Union Station on Amtrak's Southwest Chief at 7:03 a.m. Saturday and left at 10:55 a.m. on Thruway Bus 5717 to Bakersfield; anyone there from 8 a.m. to noon should monitor symptoms through Oct. 3.
  • California and Colorado health departments, working with the CDC, are notifying passengers and conducting contact tracing across both states.
  • California has recorded 59 measles cases in 13 counties this year, about 94 percent in people unvaccinated or with unknown status.

California health officials are warning of possible measles exposure across six counties after an unvaccinated passenger later hospitalized with the disease traveled through the state on Amtrak trains and connecting Thruway buses from Sept. 12 to 14. The alert comes as the United States experiences its largest measles resurgence in more than 30 years.

The California Department of Public Health said the traveler — whose identity has not been released — passed through Alameda, Butte, Kern, Los Angeles, Sacramento and San Joaquin counties. According to the department's detailed timetable, the passenger arrived in Los Angeles on Sept. 12 aboard Amtrak from Chicago, then continued on to Bakersfield, Stockton and Oroville the same day. On Sept. 13, the traveler went from Oroville to Sacramento and on to Emeryville before leaving the Bay Area for Denver on Sept. 14.

Context & Background

Measles is one of the most contagious infections known: it spreads through the air when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs or sneezes, and the virus can remain airborne for up to two hours after the person leaves. Symptoms — fever, cough, runny nose, red and watery eyes, and a characteristic rash — typically appear seven to 21 days after exposure.

The Amtrak case is part of a much larger 2026 outbreak. California has reported 59 measles cases across 13 counties this year, with roughly 94 percent in people who were unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown. Public-health experts attribute the national resurgence largely to growing vaccine hesitancy: the disease was declared eliminated in the U.S. in 2000, but coverage gaps have allowed it to roar back.

Impact & Analysis

Los Angeles County health officials issued the most specific warning on Friday: the passenger arrived at Union Station aboard Amtrak's Southwest Chief Train 3 at 7:03 a.m. Saturday and departed at 10:55 a.m. on Thruway Bus Route 5717 bound for Bakersfield. Anyone who was at Union Station between 8 a.m. and noon that day may have been exposed and should watch for symptoms through Oct. 3.

People who have had measles or received the recommended MMR vaccine are likely protected but should still monitor for symptoms, officials said. Those who are unimmunized or unsure of their status are at highest risk. Health officials advise possible contacts to check their MMR vaccination status — the vaccine can still help within 72 hours of exposure — and anyone developing symptoms should call a provider before visiting a clinic or emergency room.

"This case, along with previous measles outbreaks in California this year, serve as reminders of the importance of vaccination against measles. Measles is one of the most contagious infections that can lead to severe life-long consequences, including permanent brain damage and can also be fatal, especially for children."

— Dr. Rita Nguyen, Assistant State Public Health Officer

Diaspora Angle

Many Indian diaspora families in California travel Amtrak's routes for college drop-offs, festival trips and airport connections — and with Diwali travel season weeks away, this is a practical reminder to check vaccination cards before heading to busy stations. Families visiting relatives in India should also confirm MMR status, since international travel remains a common source of measles importation into the U.S.

What's Next

State, county and federal agencies are conducting contact tracing and notifying passengers who sat near the infected traveler. Colorado officials have separately publicized exposure windows at Denver Union Station on Sept. 15 (6–9 p.m.) and a Steamboat Springs hotel on Sept. 16. Anyone who rode the listed trains or buses — or was present at the stations on the specified dates — should monitor for symptoms for the full 21-day window and contact public health officials with questions.
